comment: Drives the home-page gallery (index.html / initScreenshotGallery in js/main.js), the press-kit build (scripts/build-press-kit.mjs), and the screenshot publish step (quotebook-ios/bin/screenshots). 'source' is the Fastlane snapshot base name emitted by UITests/SnapshotUITests.swift; bin/screenshots copies '<source>-light/-dark' from the capture output to the 'light'/'dark' filenames below. Every gallery entry names the 'platform' it belongs to; the site renders one tab per platform, in the order they appear under 'platforms'.
deviceComment: Legacy top-level field, kept because bin/widget-screenshot reads it to pick the simulator for the SpringBoard capture. It duplicates the iphone platform's 'device'; change both together.

platforms.label: iPhone
platforms.comment: Framed by `fastlane frameit` per fastlane/Framefile.json — light gets the Cosmic Orange bezel, dark gets Silver. Those bezels exist only for iPhone 17 Pro / Pro Max, which is why this device is pinned.

platforms.label: iPad
platforms.comment: Landscape, unlike the App Store set: an iPad held long-side-up is how the app is used at that size, and it fills a wide gallery slot instead of leaving a third of it empty. bin/screenshots turns this into TEST_RUNNER_QUIPS_SNAPSHOT_ORIENTATION for the capture run; SnapshotUITests rotates before navigating. The 12.9-inch is pinned rather than the newer 13-inch because frameit matches a bezel to a screenshot by exact pixel size: it knows 2732x2048 and has an iPad Pro bezel for it, but a 13-inch capture is 2752x2064 and fails with "Unsupported screen size". frameName is what bin/screenshots renames the files to before framing — frameit prefers a device matched by FILENAME over one matched by resolution, and any name containing "iPad Pro" matches the 2015 iPad Pro (home button, thick bezels) first; "ipadPro129" is the device id shared by the 3rd/4th-generation 12.9-inch, whose higher priority wins. maxWidth is ~7% above the unframed 1400 because the bezel adds that much width around the same screen.

platforms.label: Mac
platforms.comment: No simulator: the Mac shots are window captures produced by quotebook-ios/bin/mac-screenshot, which builds and runs the real app. Every mac entry is 'managed': false so bin/screenshots never overwrites them.
